summary: Okta SSO: user denied access to model-serving-dashboard after SCIM group rename
description:
Issue summary: New hire (engineer) cannot access internal model-serving-dashboard and dedicated-console after SSO login. The UI shows an authorization error immediately after successful Okta SSO redirect.

Impact: Affected user cannot perform debugging or check job queues for a live customer test; one engineer blocked. Potentially other users in the same Okta group are impacted if SCIM mapping is incorrect.

Observed behavior: After SSO sign-in the application returns HTTP 403 and shows: "Access denied: user not in required role". Okta reports a successful authentication but SCIM group sync shows failures for the renamed group.

Expected behavior: User should be assigned the "engineer:service-debug" RBAC role via Okta group membership and allowed into the consoles.

Notes: This is an internal access/RBAC issue; not a production serving outage, but blocks engineering work for the affected user.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create or use an Okta user that is a member of Corporate > Engineering > Model Serving (group id: 00gbl-OLDNAME).
2) Attempt login to https://console.redwood-inference.internal/model-serving-dashboard using Okta SSO.
3) Observe redirect to app then display of 403 authorization error.
4) Check Okta System Logs for SCIM provisioning events for the group and look for 4xx/5xx responses from /SCIM/v2/Groups endpoint.

investigation_notes: 09:20 - Reproduced locally with Aisha's account; login completes but app receives empty group set during role resolution.

09:35 - Checked Okta System Log: SCIM group rename was performed by automation on 2026-03-12 08:58 UTC. Old group id 00gbl-OLDNAME was renamed to 00gbl-NEWNAME; SCIM update queue hit rate limit and several PUTs got 429.

09:50 - Hypothesis: Rename left transient state where internal mapping table still references old Okta group id; group-sync job dropped events due to 429, so role mapping for that group wasn't updated. Result: users appear authenticated but have no RBAC roles assigned.

10:10 - Checked RBAC mapping table in Postgres: mapping row for 00gbl-OLDNAME missing; a later entry exists for 00gbl-NEWNAME but sync job did not process user->group assignment events for the interval 08:58-09:20.

10:45 - Slack thread #infra-identity: pinged Okta-admins (Marta Ruiz) and provisioning owner (J. Park). Marta confirmed Okta reported transient 429s across provisioning API due to an org-wide spike in SCIM activity from a separate migration job.
11:05 - Performed a manual role assignment as temporary unblock for ajones@redwood.com (engineer:service-debug). Documented manual step for audit.
11:30 - Created a follow-up change to increase SCIM backoff and add idempotency checks in group-sync (PR linked).

resolution: Temporary workaround: manual role assignment for affected user performed 2026-03-12 11:12 UTC. Permanent fix: increased SCIM client backoff and added idempotency/retry logic (PRs linked). Post-change reconciliation completed 2026-03-13; monitoring for missed mappings for 48h. Follow-up tasks: update runbook with the migration backoff guidance and add alerting for SCIM 4xx spikes.
notes_for_follow_up: 1) Add an alert in Datadog for OKTA_SCIM 4xx rate > 5/min. 2) Update onboarding checklist: if group rename occurs, trigger immediate full reconciliation. 3) Audit RBAC table for any users missing roles between 2026-03-12 08:45 and 2026-03-12 10:30.
